skill.name: azure-speech-to-text-rest-py
skill.description: Guides Python developers through Azure Speech to Text REST API requests for short audio files, including headers, formats, authentication, chunking, and error handling.

content.user_title: Transcribe Short Audio with Azure REST
content.value_statement: Short audio transcription requires correct Azure Speech endpoints, headers, and formats. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Python REST examples for Azure Speech to Text.
actual_capabilities: Shows required Azure Speech key and region environment variables.
Builds Python requests and aiohttp examples for short audio transcription.
Explains WAV PCM and OGG OPUS content type headers.
Covers simple and detailed response formats, profanity options, and language codes.
Demonstrates chunked upload, bearer token authentication, and status handling.
limitations: Covers the short audio REST endpoint, not batch or real-time SDK workflows.
Requires an Azure Speech resource, region, and subscription key managed by the user.
Examples assume WAV PCM or OGG OPUS audio prepared outside the skill.
Does not provide production storage, consent, logging, or compliance controls.

use_cases.title: Prototype voice input
use_cases.description: Add short spoken command transcription to a Python application using Azure Speech REST calls.

use_cases.title: Transcribe short recordings
use_cases.description: Convert brief meeting clips, notes, or test recordings into text for review.

use_cases.title: Validate Azure Speech setup
use_cases.description: Check keys, regions, content types, and response handling before building a larger integration.

prompt_templates.title: Create a minimal request
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me the minimal Python REST request for Azure Speech to Text. Use environment variables for the key and region.

prompt_templates.title: Change audio format and language
prompt_templates.prompt: Adapt the Azure Speech REST example for an OGG OPUS file in fr-FR. Include the correct content type and parameters.

prompt_templates.title: Plan response handling
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an error handling flow for Azure Speech REST transcription. Cover success, no match, bad request, unauthorized, forbidden, and service errors.

prompt_templates.title: Design production integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a production integration plan for short audio transcription with Azure Speech REST. Include chunked upload, token caching, privacy checks, and retries.

output_examples.input: Transcribe a 30 second WAV file in English.
output_examples.output: A concise Python workflow that reads the file, posts it to Azure Speech, and returns the recognized display text.

output_examples.input: Handle an unauthorized Azure Speech response.
output: Check that the subscription key is loaded from the environment.
Verify that the region matches the Azure Speech resource.
Return a clear message without printing the key or token.

output_examples.input: Compare simple and detailed recognition formats.
output_examples.output: A plain language comparison that explains display text, confidence scores, timing fields, and when to request detailed output.

best_practices: Store Azure Speech keys in environment variables or a managed secret store.
Use WAV PCM 16 kHz mono unless your service configuration supports another format.
Tell users when audio leaves the local machine for Azure processing.
anti_patterns: Do not paste subscription keys into prompts, source files, or shared logs.
Do not use this short audio endpoint for long recordings or batch jobs.
Do not send private recordings without user consent and retention rules.

faq.question: Does this skill use the Azure Speech SDK?
faq.answer: No. It shows REST requests for short audio transcription without the Speech SDK.

faq.question: How long can the audio be?
faq.answer: The documented REST endpoint is for audio up to 60 seconds. Pronunciation assessment is limited to 30 seconds.

faq.question: What credentials are required?
faq.answer: You need an Azure Speech resource key and region, stored outside prompts and source files.

faq.question: Can it provide live partial transcripts?
faq.answer: No. This REST flow returns final results only. Use the Speech SDK for live partial results.

faq.question: Does audio leave the local machine?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples send selected audio files to Azure Speech endpoints for processing.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill provides prompts and Python REST patterns that these coding agents can apply.
